subject: LLM benchmark slate, evaluation owners, and target close
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Natalie Gomez <natalie@healthgrid.io>, Sanjay Patel <sanjay@healthgrid.io>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 14 Feb 2027 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: LLm benchmark slate, evaluation owners, and target close

Hi Natalie / Sanjay — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and the proposed technical-eval MAP milestone for your team + ours. I attached an updated MAP draft and the benchmark spec workbook for the slate.

TL;DR (ask): Please confirm the evaluation owners and a target close for the technical gating milestone (proposed: 2027-03-31). Once we have owners we’ll lock the test cadence and allocate dedicated nodes for the baseline runs.

Background / goals:
- Objective: validate model quality and unit economics for the customer-facing summarization and triage flow described in the demo.
- Pass/fail will be based on the acceptance criteria below (quality + infra targets).

Proposed technical-eval milestone (one-liner):
- Deliverable: A runbook and results report demonstrating models that meet quality and performance targets on HealthGrid sample dataset (P50/P95 latency, per-token cost, and quality thresholds).
- Target close: 2027-03-31 (flexible by two weeks if security gating adds time).

Benchmarks / success criteria (from attached workbook):
- Quality: rouge-like and task F1 on prioritized prompt set: baseline target = 0.78 F1 (acceptance band 0.75–0.81).
- Latency: P95 generation latency for 512-token requests <= 180 ms on dedicated pool (95th percentile); cold-start < 400 ms.
- Throughput: sustained 90 QPS for the 8k-context baseline on a 4-GPU pool without queuing > 50 ms additional p50 latency.
- Cost: target token unit cost <= $0.0009 (end-to-end, including batching and KV caching).
- Robustness: no regression > 5% on hallucination score across the sample prompts after quantization.

Model shortlist (initial slate):
- Llama3-70B-8K (q4/ggml tuned run) — higher-quality baseline
- Mistral-7B-Instruct — fast, low-cost reference
- Falcon-40B-v2 — middle ground quality/cost

Proposed ownership & responsibilities:
- HealthGrid (owner): Natalie (technical lead) — validate dataset sampling and success criteria, provide ground-truth labels for the 200 prompt holdout.
- Redwood (owner): Karthik — run benchmark jobs, deliver results report; Priyom — security/compliance checkpoint and evidence; Marissa — model configuration and kernel tuning; Rishi — cost/quantization analysis.

Dependencies / blockers:
- HealthGrid to provide anonymized 2k-sample evaluation set and SSO access to test staging by 2027-02-21.
- Security questionnaire / SOC2 evidence requested (see Priyom’s reply below).
- Access to test VPC and bump to dedicated capacity for two-week window starting the test week.

Next steps (please reply inline):
1) Confirm Natalie/Sanjay as HealthGrid owners and who on your side will sign off on quality.
2) Confirm target close (we propose 2027-03-31).
3) Confirm you can deliver sample dataset by 2027-02-21 and whether you need a quick script to sample and anonymize.

Attachments: MAP-draft-v2.pdf (MAP with milestones), benchmark-specs.xlsx (detailed test matrix + measurement hooks)

Thanks — I’ll push a revised MAP to the Drive after we get your replies.

—
Karthik Iyer
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0132
From: Natalie Gomez <natalie@healthgrid.io>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sanjay Patel <sanjay@healthgrid.io>
Date: Mon, 15 Feb 2027 08:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: LLm benchmark slate, evaluation owners, and target close

Thanks Karthik — this is helpful. Quick answers and a couple clarifying questions: 

1) Owners: I’ll be the technical owner. Sanjay (cc’d) will be the sign-off for quality. We’ll loop in our data eng (Priya) if we need help with anonymization.
2) Target close: 2027-03-31 looks fine, but can we keep a week buffer in the plan in case of dataset gaps?
3) Dataset: we can deliver a 2k anonymized sample by 2027-02-22 (we need a sample script from you to ensure consistent formatting).

Security: We have two asks before the test VPC is spun up — a) SOC2 Type II report and b) a short data-retention summary for the staging cluster. Can Priyom point us to the material?

Also, for the model shortlist — could you include a smaller local baseline (2–4B) in the slate? We want to compare tail latency and cost trade-offs for lightweight fallbacks.

Appreciate it — Natalie
Natalie Gomez
Director, AI Platforms
HealthGrid
natalie@healthgrid.io
From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>
To: Natalie Gomez <natalie@healthgrid.io>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 15 Feb 2027 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: LLm benchmark slate, evaluation owners, and target close

Hi Natalie — welcome, and thanks for the clear asks. 

Quick security note and proposed addition to MAP:
- SOC2: attaching a short pointer pack (we don’t attach the full report in thread for security) — I’ll upload the Type II redacted summary to the Drive link in an hour and share an access token.
- Data retention for staging: default retention is 30 days for ephemeral test clusters; we can do a shorter retention or disable logging on the staging runs if you prefer. Please tell us the retention bound (7/14/30 days) and we’ll whitelist it.

MAP update suggestion: add a "Security Gate" sub-milestone under the technical-eval with owner = Priyom (deliverable: SOC2 summary + retention attestation + SSO access by 2027-02-25). This will avoid surprises before the dedicated pool is provisioned.

On the smaller-model baseline: agree — we’ll add a 3B local fallback (Alpaca-3B tuned) to the slate and include tail-latency checks.

I’ll follow up with the Drive link and the redacted SOC2 pack.

—
Priyom Das
Head of Product Security Operations
Redwood Inference
priyom@redwood.ai
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>

Date: Tue, 16 Feb 2027 11:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: LLm benchmark slate, evaluation owners, and target close

Great — thanks all. Quick updates and the small action list we’ll take from here:

Updates:
- Added Alpaca-3B (tuned) to the slate as a lightweight baseline.
- Security Gate milestone added; Priyom will drop the SOC2 pointer and retention attestation in Drive by EOD today.
- Target close: we’ll keep 2027-03-31 as the milestone and add a 1-week contingency window in the MAP (final close field = 2027-04-07).

Action list (owners):
- Natalie (HealthGrid): provide anonymized 2k sample by 2027-02-22; confirm sign-off criteria contact.
- Karthik (Redwood): schedule baseline run window and reserve dedicated pool (proposed week of 2027-03-07).
- Priyom (Redwood): deliver SOC2 pointer + retention attestation by 2027-02-16.
- Marissa (Redwood): prepare kernel/quantization config and runbook by 2027-03-01.
- Rishi (Redwood): run cost analysis and produce per-model unit economics by 2027-03-20.

If that looks good I’ll commit the MAP to the Drive and push an updated milestone tracker to the HubSpot record (HG-2027-07).

Thanks — looking forward to progressing.

—
Karthik
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
